title: Scheduler integration and end-to-end profiling playbook
author: Asha Kapoor
content:
Overview

This playbook documents an end-to-end procedure for integrating scheduler-level signals with kernel and runtime profiling to diagnose performance regressions, validate scheduler changes, and produce deterministic benchmarking artifacts. It covers required telemetry, experiment templates, step-by-step collection recipes, analysis heuristics, SLO checks, and incident/runbook guidance. The intended audience is runtime engineers, scheduler authors, SREs, and performance QA.

Scope and goals

- Scope: production and staging runtime clusters, kernel scheduler variants (e.g., preemptive handoff, admission-controller tweaks), and profiling pipelines that touch GPU/CPU kernel execution, KV cache behavior, and request multiplexing.
- Goals:
  - Provide a repeatable profiling and benchmarking workflow that links scheduler decisions -> kernel execution metrics -> end-to-end latency distribution.
  - Define minimal telemetry contract and collection commands so experiments are comparable across hardware and model variants.
  - Produce artifacts for regression triage (trace bundles, synthetic replay, and a short summary report).

When to use this playbook

1. After a scheduler change (policy or implementation) that touches admission, preemption, or batch slicing.
2. When a P95/P99 latency regression is observed after release.
3. Prior to a canary rollout of a scheduler or kernel change.
4. During capacity planning or hardware-fit experiments.

High-level architecture impact

- Scheduler decisions should carry a deterministic context token (scheduler_decision_id) that is injected into request provenance and all downstream traces.
- The decision token must propagate to kernel dispatch layers, runtime traces, and exporter annotations. This allows trace correlation across layers without manual mapping.
- Telemetry producer components: request-gateway, admission-controller, kernel-dispatcher, kvcache-shard, and kernel-runner.

Minimal telemetry contract (required fields)

Each sampled trace must include the following fields (as tags/fields):
- trace_id (string)
- request_id (string)
- scheduler_decision_id (string)
- cohort (string) — e.g., canary|control|baseline|experiment
- model_variant (string)
- kernel_variant (string)
- gpu_id / cpu_node (string)
- seq_len (int)
- token_count (int)
- enqueue_time, dispatch_time, kernel_start_time, kernel_end_time, response_write_time (ISO timestamps)
- batch_size (int)
- admission_reason (string) — e.g., immediate, queued, preempted, hedged

Suggested additional metrics (histograms / counters):
- kernel_exec_ms (histogram) - kernel execution duration per request
- enqueue_ms, queue_wait_ms (histogram)
- kvcache_hit_rate (gauge) per tenant/cohort
- kernel_retry_count (counter)
- scheduler_action_counts{action} (counter)

Collection and tooling prerequisites

- Tracing: Jaeger-compatible traces with 100% decision token sampling for scheduled experiments.
- Kernel traces: nsys (NVIDIA Nsight) or ROCm tracing for AMD, plus lightweight per-kernel timing exposed via runtime counters.
- Profiler builds: builds instrumented for timeline annotations (build tag: prof/annotated-2026*).
- Replay harness: request-surface-replayer v2.1 or later.
- Central artifact store: s3://redwood-perf/artifacts/{experiment}/{date}/

Standard experiment template (single file: experiment.yaml)

Example experiment metadata (YAML):

experiment_name: scheduler-hand-off-microburst-2026-02-01
description: Measure tail-latency impact of preemptive handoff under microburst traffic for llama-13b-quant
cohorts:
  - control: scheduler:stable, kernel:baseline, cohort:control
  - experiment: scheduler:preemptive-hand-off-v3, kernel:baseline, cohort:experiment
traffic_profile: microburst-1s-on-9s-off
model_variant: llama-13b-quant
sequence_distribution: p(<=64)=0.7, p(65-256)=0.25, p(256+)=0.05
collect_traces: true
trace_sample_rate: 1.0
artifact_bucket: s3://redwood-perf/artifacts/scheduler-hand-off-microburst-2026-02-01/

Step-by-step collection recipe (canonical)

1) Prepare baseline: pin control cohort to scheduler:stable and kernel:baseline. Verify canary isolation (no cross-cohort mixing).
2) Start the replay harness against staging cluster with the defined traffic_profile. Use request-surface-replayer with injected request_id and scheduler_decision_id:

# run from perf workstation
request-surface-replayer --experiment experiment.yaml --outdir /tmp/exp-run --inject-decision-token

3) Start system-level collectors (run on all nodes hosting kernel-runner processes):
- Start nsys for GPU: sudo nsys profile -o /tmp/nsys-${NODE}.qdrep --sample=cpu,gpu --trace=nvtx --duration=600s --capture=all
- Start cpu perf or eBPF sampler: sudo perf record -F 99 -a -g -o /tmp/perf-${NODE}.data sleep 600
- Start lightweight runtime exporter: curl -X POST http://localhost:9001/debug/trace/start?out=/tmp/trace-${NODE}.ndjson

4) Start distributed trace capture (Jaeger) with 100% sampling for the experiment cohort.
5) Run the replay for configured duration (recommended 10–30 minutes for microburst experiments).
6) After run completes, collect artifacts from nodes and upload to experiment artifact bucket following naming convention: {experiment}/{cohort}/{node}/{timestamp}/trace.qdrep, perf.data, runtime-trace.ndjson, jaeger-trace.json

Analysis heuristics (quick triage)

- Correlate scheduler_decision_id with kernel_exec_ms from kernel traces. Create a pivot table: scheduler_action -> median kernel_exec_ms, p95 kernel_exec_ms, mean queue_wait_ms.
- Look for cohorts where kernel_start_time is significantly delayed relative to dispatch_time (>10 ms baseline depending on model shape).
- If kernel_exec_ms variance grows with batch_size, inspect batch-slicing/handoff logs for cross-tenant batching.
- If eBPF/perf shows system-level scheduling preemption spikes coincident with high p99, search for SIGSTOP/SIGCONT patterns or GPU watchdog resets.

Automated checks and SLO gates

Before a scheduler change is promoted to production, these automated checks must pass in staging: 
- Regression-free on p50/p95/p99 for baseline workload within 5%/8%/12% respectively.
- Kernel retry rate increase < 2% absolute.
- kvcache_hit_rate delta < 1% (unless expected).
- No increase in scheduler_action_counts{preempt} > 3x baseline without documented rationale.

Alerting rules (sample)

- alert: SchedulerTailLatencyRegression
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(kernel_exec_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le, cohort)) > 1.12 * baseline_p99
  for: 10m
  labels: {severity: page}

- alert: KernelRetrySpike
  expr: increase(kernel_retry_count[5m]) > 100 && increase(kernel_retry_count[5m]) / increase(request_count[5m]) > 0.02
  for: 5m
  labels: {severity: ticket}

Rollout checklist (pre-canary)

- [ ] Experiment YAML committed to repo and pinned to artifact bucket.
- [ ] Tracing + kernel trace infrastructure smoke-tested.
- [ ] Baseline run completed and artifact snapshot stored.
- [ ] Owners & oncall notified (Slack #serving-runtime with experiment tag).
- [ ] Canary policy configured (5% of traffic for 30 minutes -> 25% for 1h -> 100% with rollback).
- [ ] SLO gates configured in deployment pipeline.

Runbook: triage flow for observed tail-latency regression

1) Verify alert source and cohort. If cohort != canary and no rollout in progress, page oncall.
2) Fetch experiment artifact bundle and open the summary report (artifact/{experiment}/summary.json). Key fields: delta_p99, median_queue_wait_ms, kernel_retry_rate.
3) Cross-correlate scheduler_decision_id for top 10 slow traces and inspect kernel qdrep slices at those timestamps.
4) Check node-level telemetry: GPU utilization, nvlink errors, dmesg, OOM/killer events, and GPU watchdog messages.
5) If traces show kernel_start_time delayed but steady kernel_exec_ms, suspect admission latency or queueing; escalate to scheduler owner.
6) If kernel_exec_ms inflated and kernels show >1.5x expected occupancy drift, open a kernel regression issue and attach qdrep.
7) If system-level indicators show GPU thermal throttling, coordinate with SRE to move canary to alternate hardware.

Known issues and mitigations (short catalog)

- mis-attributed-decision-token: Some legacy gateway versions drop scheduler_decision_id when requests are proxied through legacy route. Mitigation: enforce gateway version >= 2025.11 and run injector sidecar for older routes.
- perf-sampling-sparsity-on-high-throughput: perf recorder under-samples when node CPU is saturated; mitigation: reduce sampling frequency and increase test duration for stability.
- nsys-file-size-bloat: long runs generate large qdrep files; mitigation: use time-windowed capture and aggregate smaller windows with qdrep-concat.

Release notes (summary of recent changes relevant to this playbook)

- 2026-01-10: scheduler:preemptive-hand-off-v3 landed. The new policy reduces starvation but introduced additional preempt events; this playbook includes a specific experiment template to quantify the latency impact under microbursts.
- 2025-12-03: runtime:annotated-prof builds published; these include NVTX span annotations for scheduler_decision_id and batch lineage. Use these builds for kernel-level correlation.

Ownership and escalation

- Primary owners: Serving Runtime - Scheduling subteam (owner alias: runtime-scheduler@redwood.com).
- SRE escalation: eng-sre-oncall@redwood.com.
- Performance lab contact: perf-lab@redwood.com.

Artifact naming and retention policy

- Naming: {experiment}/{cohort}/{node}/{YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS}/{artifact}.{ext}
- Retention: experiments used for production rollouts retained for 365 days. Debug/ephemeral experiments may be retained for 30 days. Critical regression runs (P99 delta > 10%) archived indefinitely.

Appendix A — useful commands and snippets

Collecting a short GPU slice with nsys:

sudo nsys profile -o /tmp/qdrep --capture=nvtx,cuda,nvtx --sample=cpu,gpu --duration=60s --trace=nvtx --quiet

Extracting timeline to JSON (local):

nsys stats --report gputimeline --format json /tmp/qdrep.qdrep > /tmp/qdrep.timeline.json

Quick pivot using jq and python (example):

jq -c '.[] | select(.tags.scheduler_decision_id != null) | {trace_id: .trace_id, decision: .tags.scheduler_decision_id, kernel_ms: .metrics.kernel_exec_ms}' jaeger-trace.json | python -c 'import sys, json; data=[json.loads(l) for l in sys.stdin]; print(len(data))'

Experiment result template (copy into artifact summary.json)

- experiment: string
- cohort: string
- p50_control, p95_control, p99_control: ms
- p50_experiment, p95_experiment, p99_experiment: ms
- delta_p99_percent: float
- kernel_retry_rate_control, kernel_retry_rate_experiment: float
- notes: string (root cause hypothesis)

Feedback and continuous improvement

- Add new experiment templates to this page and tag with the date.
- After each canary, the owner must add a short summary to the experiment artifact and tag whether the SLO gate passed.
